record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.context_brief: Recovering a curve from lattice-hit data
record.original_question: Let C be a curve in R^2 and fix an ε-sized square lattice. As the curve translates, record the translation parameters λ for which the curve passes through a lattice point. Can one recover the shape of C from this resulting distribution of click times, for arbitrary ε > 0, and at least in the easier variant where the data are available not only for C but also for all rotations of C?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Can one recover the shape of the curve given this distribution of points for any ε > 0 (presumably only small ε are needed, of course) for the curve C? Or – an easier question – for the curve and for all of its rotations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth curve, and fix $\varepsilon > 0$. Consider the square lattice $\varepsilon \mathbb{Z}^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$. For a parameter $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}^2$, let $C + \lambda$ denote the translate of $C$ by $\lambda$, and define the "click set"
$$S_\varepsilon(C) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{R}^2 : (C + \lambda) \cap \varepsilon \mathbb{Z}^2 \neq \emptyset\},$$
together with its natural multiplicity/density structure (each $\lambda$ recorded as many times as there are lattice points on $C + \lambda$).

(a) Given the data $S_\varepsilon(C)$ for some (or all sufficiently small) $\varepsilon > 0$, is it possible to reconstruct the shape of $C$ up to rigid motion?

(b) Easier variant: given the family of click sets $\{S_\varepsilon(R_\theta C) : \theta \in [0, 2\pi)\}$ obtained from all rotations $R_\theta C$ of the curve, can the shape of $C$ be recovered?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a compiled list of open problems on billiards and geometric optics and is stated as an open question, with only heuristic remarks (asymptotic patterns near rational slopes encode curvature). No subsequent publication resolving it was found.
